part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: But at night, while they lay sleeping, came down on them terrible men, who lived with the bears in the mountains, like Titans or giants in shape; for each of them had six arms, and they fought with young firs and pines.  But Heracles killed them all before morn with his deadly poisoned arrows; but among them, in the darkness, he slew Cyzicus the kindly prince.

translation.en: But at night, while they lay sleeping, terrible men came down on them from the mountains.
translation.kr: 하지만 밤이 되어 그들이 잠든 사이, 산에서 끔찍한 사내들이 습격해 왔습니다.

translation.en: These men lived with the bears and looked like Titans or giants.
translation.kr: 이들은 곰들과 함께 살았으며 마치 타이탄이나 거인 같은 모습이었습니다.

translation.en: Each of them had six arms, and they fought using young fir and pine trees as weapons.
translation.kr: 모두 여섯 개의 팔을 가졌고, 어린 전나무와 소나무를 무기 삼아 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: Before morning, Heracles killed them all with his deadly poisoned arrows.
translation.kr: 날이 밝기 전, 헤라클레스는 치명적인 독화살로 그들을 모두 쓰러뜨렸습니다.

translation.en: Tragically, in the darkness, he also slew the kindly prince Cyzicus.
translation.kr: 하지만 비극적이게도 어둠 속에서 그만 친절한 왕자 키지코스까지 죽이고 말았습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then they got to their ship and to their oars, and Tiphys bade them cast off the hawsers and go to sea.  But as he spoke a whirlwind came, and spun the _Argo_ round, and twisted the hawsers together, so that no man could loose them.  Then Tiphys dropped the rudder from his hand, and cried, This comes from the Gods above.  But Jason went forward, and asked counsel of the magic bough.

translation.en: Then they returned to their ship and took to their oars.
translation.kr: 그 후 일행은 배로 돌아가 노를 잡았습니다.

translation.en: Tiphys ordered them to cast off the ropes and head out to sea.
translation.kr: 티피스는 밧줄을 풀고 바다로 나가라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: But as he spoke, a whirlwind spun the Argo around and twisted the ropes tightly together.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 말하는 순간 회오리바람이 불어와 아르고호를 회전시켰고, 밧줄을 단단히 꼬아버렸습니다.

translation.en: No man could loosen them.
translation.kr: 아무도 그 밧줄을 풀 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: Tiphys dropped the rudder from his hand and cried, This comes from the Gods above.
translation.kr: 티피스는 손에서 방향타를 놓으며, 이것은 하늘의 신들이 내린 일이라고 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Jason went forward and asked the magic bough for guidance.
translation.kr: 이아손은 앞으로 나아가 마법의 나뭇가지에게 조언을 구했습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Then the magic bough spoke, and answered, This is because you have slain Cyzicus your friend.  You must appease his soul, or you will never leave this shore.

translation.en: The magic bough answered, This is because you have slain your friend Cyzicus.
translation.kr: 마법의 나뭇가지가 대답하기를, 이것은 당신들이 친구인 키지코스를 죽였기 때문이라고 했습니다.

translation.en: You must appease his soul, or you will never leave this shore.
translation.kr: 그의 영혼을 달래주지 않으면 결코 이 해안을 떠날 수 없을 것이라고도 했습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: Jason went back sadly, and told the heroes what he had heard.  And they leapt on shore, and searched till dawn; and at dawn they found the body, all rolled in dust and blood, among the corpses of those monstrous beasts.  And they wept over their kind host, and laid him on a fair bed, and heaped a huge mound over him, and offered black sheep at his tomb, and Orpheus sang a magic song to him, that his spirit might have rest. And then they held games at the tomb, after the custom of those times, and Jason gave prizes to each winner.  To Ancus he gave a golden cup, for he wrestled best of all; and to Heracles a silver one, for he was the strongest of all; and to Castor, who rode best, a golden crest; and Polydeuces the boxer had a rich carpet, and to Orpheus for his song a sandal with golden wings.  But Jason himself was the best of all the archers, and the Minuai crowned him with an olive crown; and so, the songs say, the soul of good Cyzicus was appeased and the heroes went on their way in peace.

translation.en: Jason went back sadly and told the heroes what he had heard.
translation.kr: 이아손은 슬픈 얼굴로 돌아와 영웅들에게 자신이 들은 이야기를 전했습니다.

translation.en: They leapt onto the shore and searched until dawn.
translation.kr: 그들은 해안으로 뛰어내려 동이 틀 때까지 찾아 헤매었습니다.

translation.en: At dawn they found the body, covered in dust and blood, among the corpses of the monstrous beasts.
translation.kr: 새벽녘에 그들은 괴물 같은 짐승들의 시체 사이에서 먼지와 피투성이가 된 시신을 발견했습니다.

translation.en: They wept over their kind host and laid him on a beautiful bed.
translation.kr: 그들은 친절했던 주인을 위해 눈물을 흘리며 그를 아름다운 침상에 뉘었습니다.

translation.en: They heaped a huge mound over him and offered black sheep at his tomb.
translation.kr: 그 위로 거대한 흙무덤을 쌓아 올리고, 무덤 앞에서 검은 양을 제물로 바쳤습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus sang a magic song to him, so that his spirit might find rest.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 그의 영혼이 안식을 찾을 수 있도록 마법의 노래를 불렀습니다.

translation.en: Then they held funeral games at the tomb, following the custom of those times.
translation.kr: 그리고 그 시절의 관습에 따라 무덤 곁에서 장례 경기를 열었습니다.

translation.en: Jason gave prizes to each winner.
translation.kr: 이아손은 각 경기의 우승자에게 상을 주었습니다.

translation.en: He gave a golden cup to Ancaeus, who wrestled the best.
translation.kr: 씨름을 가장 잘한 안카이오스에게는 황금 잔을 주었습니다.

translation.en: Heracles received a silver cup, as he was the strongest of all.
translation.kr: 가장 힘이 셌던 헤라클레스는 은 잔을 받았습니다.

translation.en: Castor, who rode best, won a golden crest.
translation.kr: 승마 솜씨가 제일 뛰어났던 카스토르는 황금 장식을 받았습니다.

translation.en: Polydeuces the boxer received a rich carpet.
translation.kr: 권투 선수인 폴리데우케스는 화려한 양탄자를 차지했습니다.

translation.en: Orpheus was rewarded with a golden-winged sandal for his song.
translation.kr: 오르페우스는 노래에 대한 보답으로 황금 날개가 달린 샌들을 받았습니다.

translation.en: But Jason himself was the best of all the archers.
translation.kr: 하지만 이아손 자신이 모든 궁수 중 가장 뛰어났습니다.

translation.en: The Minyans crowned him with an olive wreath.
translation.kr: 미니아스인들은 그에게 올리브 화관을 씌워 주었습니다.

translation.en: Thus, the songs say, the soul of good Cyzicus was appeased.
translation.kr: 전해지는 노래에 따르면, 이리하여 선량한 키지코스의 영혼이 달래졌다고 합니다.

translation.en: The heroes then went on their way in peace.
translation.kr: 그 후 영웅들은 평온하게 길을 떠났습니다.

part: Part IV: How the Argonauts Sailed to Colchis
raw: But when Cyzicus wife heard that he was dead she died likewise of grief; and her tears became a fountain of clear water, which flows the whole year round.

translation.en: When Cyzicus's wife heard that he was dead, she died of grief as well.
translation.kr: 남편이 죽었다는 소식을 들은 키지코스의 아내 역시 슬픔을 이기지 못하고 세상을 떠났습니다.

translation.en: Her tears became a fountain of clear water, which flows year-round.
translation.kr: 그녀의 눈물은 맑은 샘물이 되어 일 년 내내 흐르고 있습니다.
